findings.summary: The first-visit experience ignores the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in treatment to the light capture: a white full-screen surface remains under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens, including the consent layer.

findings.summary: Infinite pulse animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports 18 running pulse-19bfe654 animations, each 3000ms and infinite, while the media query matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential pulse animations inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Text/UI contrast is insufficient in the default experience.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audit fails and the overall accessibility score is 0.84.
findings.suggestedFix: Use contrast-safe color tokens and test default, prefers-contrast and forced-colors states.

findings.summary: Route/state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered CSS/DOM probe found no active View Transition declarations or API usage on a highly navigational news site.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same- and cross-document navigation with View Transitions while preserving no-motion behavior.

findings.summary: A full-screen pay-or-track gateway obscures every sampled public-content path.
findings.evidence: Desktop/mobile captures of home, section, article and Directs show subscription choices plus “accept cookies … free”; refusal warns that navigation/features are limited. Core news is not visible in the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with non-obscuring, equal-choice consent controls and keep public core content usable without personalized tracking.

findings.summary: The modal gateway is implemented as custom div-based UI rather than a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM recon found a DIV modal surface and no <dialog>; the full-screen interaction requires custom handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with correct modal semantics, initial focus, Escape behavior and an equally prominent non-consent action.

findings.summary: No component-level container queries were found.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found logical properties but no active @container rule across a card-heavy, reused-component layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries where cards/widgets are reused across rails and viewport regions; keep media-query fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and some controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing a link, computed outline was none and box-shadow none; sampled 32px controls are below a comfortable 44px target.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment and increase interactive target hit areas.

findings.summary: JavaScript work remains heavy despite acceptable paint timing.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 3.5s main-thread work, 1.6s JS execution and 339ms TBT; HAR records 132 script requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove/conditional-load heavy scripts, chunk long work, and defer non-essential tags until consent and interaction.

findings.summary: The initial dependency graph is script-heavy.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 236 requests and 2.16MB transferred, including 132 scripts and 54 stylesheets; Lighthouse flags font display and the dependency tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, preload only true LCP dependencies, use font-display, and delay non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Third-party and first-party JavaScript dominates initial delivery.
findings.evidence: Scripts transfer 1.42MB; top offenders include GTM, Permutive, Didomi, Google sign-in and the 195KB vendor bundle before content access.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to remove unused vendor code and load analytics, ads and identity providers only when required and permitted.

findings.summary: Accessible names and alternatives are missing.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails button-name, link-name and image-alt; image probe reports 35 images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable control a discernible name and meaningful images appropriate alt; use empty alt only for decoration.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and accessibility-tree structure fail.
findings.evidence: The focused-link probe shows no visible focus style; Lighthouse reports a malformed accessibility tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair landmark/heading relationships and implement consistent visible focus in logical DOM order.

findings.summary: Some targets do not meet inclusive target-size expectations.
findings.evidence: The viewport allows up to 5× zoom and mobile has no overflow, but sampled controls are 32px high, below a comfortable touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px without changing visual icon size.

findings.summary: Browser errors occur during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console audit scores 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the recorded console/network errors and add production monitoring for uncaught exceptions.

findings.summary: Image markup and responsive delivery are weak.
findings.evidence: Image probe reports 91/100 missing width or height attributes, 45 missing srcset, 51 legacy-format images and 3 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes and modern encodings from the image pipeline.

findings.summary: DevTools platform hygiene checks fail.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript and Inspector Issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish correct production source maps to authorized tooling and clear all DevTools Issues/deprecations.

findings.summary: robots.txt blocks all generic crawlers despite public indexable metadata.
findings.evidence: robots.txt starts with User-agent: * / Disallow: / and only grants broad access to named search engines; generic and AI crawlers cannot crawl the 95–97% SSR content.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace default-deny with explicit policy aligned to intended public discovery, while retaining targeted exclusions.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: CSP is only “block-all-mixed-content”; Permissions-Policy is absent; two first-party cookies are not Secure and several use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based allowlist CSP, Secure cookies with least-permissive SameSite, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: A large tracking/third-party surface loads on the consent wall.
findings.evidence: Tracker probe finds 15 third-party origins including GTM and Google Ads; HAR attributes 24 requests and 694,639 bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential third parties until affirmative granular consent and reduce vendors, event volume and retention.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced policy headers are incomplete or weak.
findings.evidence: Permissions-Policy is absent, Referrer-Policy is legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade, and CSP has no source allowlist/frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrictive Permissions-Policy, strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and frame-ancestors in CSP.

findings.summary: Install/offline plumbing is incomplete.
findings.evidence: A service worker is active and /manifest.json exists, but no manifest link was found in the page and Cache Storage was empty after load; no offline fallback was evidenced.
findings.suggestedFix: Link the manifest and have the service worker cache a small offline fallback plus core shell assets.

findings.summary: Free access is conditioned on accepting personalized advertising trackers.
findings.evidence: The gateway says users must accept personalized-ad trackers from L’Équipe and 278 partners for free access and that refusal limits navigation/features.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer a genuinely equivalent reject path, avoid conditioning core content on personalized tracking, and present choices with equal prominence.

findings.summary: Empty login submission gives no visible or programmatic recovery feedback.
findings.evidence: After submitting the empty sign-in form, the probe found no :invalid fields, role=alert content, or error message.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints, validate after interaction, focus the first invalid field and announce a concise error through a live region.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit labels and autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found pseudo and password inputs with no associated label and empty autocomplete attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add persistent labels and autocomplete=username/current-password; preserve paste and password-manager support.

findings.summary: The sampled sign-in flow exposes only password/social sign-in, not phishing-resistant passkeys.
findings.evidence: Account DOM contains username/password fields and Apple/Google actions; no WebAuthn/passkey affordance was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in/registration alongside recovery-safe existing methods; request permissions only after user intent.

findings.summary: The first screen prioritizes subscription before clear terms or an equivalent free path.
findings.evidence: The gateway leads with “je m’abonne” and Google subscription, while pricing/commitment details are not visible and free access requires tracking consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Show price, renewal and cancellation terms before commitment and provide a clear account/cancellation route.

findings.summary: The image estate is not resource-efficient.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 51 use legacy formats, 45 lack srcset and 3 are oversized; many have no intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants with width-based srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Substantial analytics/ad work occurs before core content is available.
findings.evidence: The consent screen load still makes 236 requests with 132 scripts and known tracking vendors.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate and batch background analytics, eliminate duplicate tag loads and defer low-value work to idle/user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party script cost is disproportionate on the initial wall.
findings.evidence: Third parties transfer 694KB; GTM alone transfers 241KB and several vendors take around one second.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors and lazy-load approved integrations.

findings.summary: The initial page has a large DOM/heap footprint for a consent-gated first view.
findings.evidence: Heap summary reports 810,415 nodes and 47.76MB self size before interaction; after ten menu toggles it reaches 816,629 nodes and 48.19MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce hidden/pre-rendered DOM and vendor allocations; profile retained objects and detached nodes on representative navigation.
